Two pods, `api-7d4b6f6f7d-m29sh` and `api-7d4b6f6f7d-ng552`, were observed at 1/2 Ready with STATUS=OOMKilled and 3 restarts within ~55-57 seconds of pod start [5]. The `api` application container in each pod remained healthy (Running, Ready: True, 0 restarts), while a second container, `log-shipper`, was repeatedly Terminated with Reason OOMKilled, Exit Code 137 [7]. The Deployment's status showed 3 desired replicas with only 1 ready and 2 unavailable, failing its minimum-availability condition [8, 14]. All other shop namespace workloads (frontend, worker, redis, loadgen) remained healthy with 0 restarts [5].

**Root Cause**

The root cause is confirmed. A rollout to revision 2 of the shop/api Deployment introduced a new `log-shipper` sidecar container that is not present in the prior revision 1 ReplicaSet (`api-f64486c4c`, which contains only the single `api` container) [8, 11]. The `log-shipper` container's startup code immediately allocates a 40 MB in-memory buffer, as confirmed by its own log output ("buffering 40 MB before first flush") [12], against a configured container memory limit of only 16Mi [7]. This oversized allocation relative to the limit causes the kubelet to OOMKill the container on every start (Exit Code 137, Restart Count 3) [7], placing the pod's `log-shipper` container into a crash loop that keeps the overall pod at 1/2 Ready and the Deployment below its minimum-availability threshold — the mechanism directly responsible for the KubePodCrashLooping alert [8, 14]. The primary `api` application container is unaffected by this condition [7].

**Impact & Timeline**

Of the Deployment's 3 desired replicas, 2 pods (`api-7d4b6f6f7d-m29sh`, `api-7d4b6f6f7d-ng552`) running revision 2 are actively crash-looping with 1/2 Ready status, while a third pod on the prior revision 1 ReplicaSet (`api-f64486c4c-fkwbq`) remains fully healthy at 1/1 Ready [5, 14]. Because the `api` application container itself continues to serve traffic in all pods, including the two affected ones, user-facing impact is likely limited to reduced capacity/redundancy rather than full service outage, though the Deployment cannot reach its desired replica count until remediated [7, 8].

- Node-level resource pressure — all 3 cluster nodes report Ready status [13], and other pods scheduled on the same nodes (frontend, worker, redis, loadgen) show 0 restarts and stable Ready status [5].
- Application/Redis-level failure in the `api` container — the `api` container itself is Running, Ready: True, with 0 restarts, indicating the application logic and its dependencies are functioning normally [7].

The pod `worker-86f68b9bf6-t2rwq` was observed in a crash loop, repeatedly terminating with OOMKilled (exit code 137) and entering BackOff [5]. Cluster events show two worker ReplicaSets were created roughly 9 seconds apart immediately prior to the alert: `worker-6cf88d4b58` (revision 1) was scaled up and then down to 0 replicas, while `worker-86f68b9bf6` (revision 2) was scaled up to become the active ReplicaSet [6, 7]. Other `shop` services (api, frontend) were running normally (1/1 Ready) at the time of investigation and were not affected [3].

**Root Cause**

The root cause was a deployment rollout that increased the worker's `BATCH_SIZE` environment variable from 500 to 2500 without a corresponding increase to the pod's 192Mi memory limit [7]. The worker's code allocates `BATCH_SIZE × 100KiB` of buffer per cycle [10]; at BATCH_SIZE=2500 this requires approximately 244MiB, which exceeds the unchanged 192Mi memory limit before accounting for interpreter overhead, resulting in a guaranteed OOMKill on every cycle [10, 7]. This directly explains the observed OOMKilled terminations and restart behavior on `worker-86f68b9bf6-t2rwq` [5]. The prior ReplicaSet (revision 1, BATCH_SIZE=500, same 192Mi limit) remains present in-cluster at 0 replicas and was not garbage-collected, confirming it as a valid, intact rollback target [7].

**Impact & Timeline**

Revision 1 (`worker-6cf88d4b58`) was created at 14:39:07 and scaled down roughly 9 seconds later as revision 2 (`worker-86f68b9bf6`, BATCH_SIZE=2500) was created at 14:39:16 and scaled up [6, 7]. The affected pod subsequently entered a crash loop, with OOMKilled terminations recorded at 14:39:57 and 14:40:40, reaching a restart count of 4 and BackOff status by the time of investigation [5]. tool_input.title: shop/frontend KubeDeploymentRolloutStuck - image tag typo (rev2)
tool_input.content:
## Symptom
KubeDeploymentRolloutStuck alert on shop/frontend. `kubectl get deployment frontend -n shop` shows READY 2/2 but UP-TO-DATE < desired (e.g. 1/2). Old ReplicaSet pods stay healthy; new ReplicaSet pod sits at 0/1 Ready.

## Root cause (confirmed 2026-10-02)
Deployment revision 2's pod template image was set to `nginx:1.27-alpne` (typo, missing "i" — should be `nginx:1.27-alpine`). This tag does not exist on Docker Hub, so the new ReplicaSet's pod permanently sits in `ImagePullBackOff` (`kubectl describe pod` → "failed to resolve reference ... not found").

Diagnostic tell: `kubectl get deployment frontend -o yaml` → the `kubectl.kubernetes.io/last-applied-configuration` annotation shows the CORRECT image (from the original `apply`), but the live `spec.template.spec.containers[0].image` has the typo. This mismatch proves the bad image was introduced via an imperative command (e.g. `kubectl set image deployment/frontend nginx=nginx:1.27-alpne`) rather than a tracked `apply`, bypassing config review.

Because RollingUpdate `maxUnavailable: 25%` on 2 replicas rounds to 0, the old (healthy) ReplicaSet is never scaled down until the new pod is Ready — which never happens — so the Deployment gets permanently stuck at updatedReplicas < desired, unavailableReplicas > 0, triggering the alert. User impact is minimal since old pods keep serving.

## Diagnosis steps
1. `kubectl get deployment frontend -n shop -o wide` — check READY vs UP-TO-DATE vs AVAILABLE.
2. `kubectl get rs -n shop -l app=frontend -o wide` — compare IMAGES column across ReplicaSets by revision.
3. `kubectl describe pod <new-rs-pod> -n shop` — look for ImagePullBackOff / ErrImagePull and the exact failed image string.
4. `kubectl get deployment frontend -o yaml` — diff last-applied-configuration annotation image vs live spec image to spot imperative-edit typos.

## Validated fixes (both require write access, blocked under read-only policy)
- Fix-forward: `kubectl set image deployment/frontend nginx=nginx:1.27-alpine -n shop` — image already cached on cluster nodes (confirmed via events "already present on machine"), so pulls instantly.
- Rollback: `kubectl rollout undo deployment/frontend -n shop` — rev-1 ReplicaSet confirmed intact and healthy (2/2 Ready) at diagnosis time.

## Prevention
Avoid imperative `kubectl set image`/edits for image tag changes — they bypass the last-applied-configuration diffing that would otherwise make an image typo visible in a `kubectl diff`/PR review. Prefer GitOps/`kubectl apply` from reviewed manifests.
